# Copilot instructions

## Technology preferences

- Prefer the latest currently supported .NET LTS release for new tools, utilities, and systems.
- If .NET is not a practical fit, prefer Node.js and JavaScript.
- Avoid Python for new tooling when .NET or Node.js can meet the requirement; use Python only when an existing tool or a clear technical constraint makes it the better fit.
- Follow existing repository architecture and explicit project requirements when they call for a different technology.

## Cost and approvals

- Prefer free/zero marginal cost when it is commercially permitted, secure, credible, and portable.
- Do not incur new incremental spend without Cyrus's explicit approval first. This includes metered AI/model usage, API calls, cloud resources, paid tiers, and subscriptions.
- Before asking for approval, state the provider, one-time and recurring costs, usage assumptions, free alternatives, data/privacy/security implications, and teardown or cancellation path. Stop before incurring the cost.
- Use already-approved entitlements with cost-aware defaults; avoid unnecessary agent spawns, duplicate work, and parallelism that does not shorten delivery.
